findings.motion: HB 958 Election Law Changes, Senate second reading, roll call 693
findings.note: Senate roll call 693 lists Settle among the Ayes (28 to 13). The ratified bill text (https://www.ncleg.gov/Sessions/2025/Bills/House/PDF/H958v9.pdf) stops a drivers license office or county board from processing a voter registration unless the applicant affirmatively states U.S. citizenship, requires a sworn citizenship statement if the answer is blank, and sends DMV data and federal database matches on possible non-citizens to the State Board for removal from the rolls. The bill page shows the Governor vetoed it. The member vote list shows no separate Settle entry for a third-reading vote.

findings.motion: HB 958 Election Law Changes, Senate Amendment 1, roll call 684
findings.note: Senate roll call 684 lists Settle among the Ayes on Amendment 1 to HB 958 (31 to 11). The member vote list shows him voting Aye on the other HB 958 amendment and table motions the same evening (roll calls 685 to 692).

findings.motion: SB 88 Various Elections Changes, Senate third reading, roll call 620
findings.note: Roll call 620 lists Settle among the Ayes (28 to 19). The third edition (https://www.ncleg.gov/Sessions/2023/Bills/Senate/PDF/S88v3.pdf) requires county boards to challenge ballots of voters ineligible through death or felony conviction and requires signature verification software on executed absentee ballots.

findings.motion: SB 352 Remove Foreign Citizens from Voting Rolls, listed as a sponsor (not primary)
findings.note: The bill page lists Settle among the sponsors, with Burgin as primary. Filed 3/22/2023 and sent to committee 3/23/2023, no further action. The bill text (https://www.ncleg.gov/Sessions/2023/Bills/Senate/PDF/S352v0.pdf) makes U.S. citizenship a juror requirement and has court-excuse forms on non-citizenship shared with the State Board of Elections.

findings.motion: SB 88 Various Elections Changes, listed as a sponsor (not primary)
findings.note: The bill page lists Settle among the sponsors, with Hise as primary. The bill was filed February 13, 2023. It covers voter-roll ballot challenges and signature verification on absentee ballots.
